title: Property Pack: information, meaning and review
notebookTitle: OPDA | Property Pack learning media | Private local review 2026-10-26

review.scope: Complete authored readings, selected original bodies, provenance, prompts and native settings; current candidate and proposed decisions remain qualified.
review.authority: Owner-commissioned implementation and generation; local review only.

sections.title: Understanding the Property Pack
sections.purpose: Connect the transaction's information needs with the model, its semantic homes and the evidence required for review.
sections.audience: Property professionals, domain reviewers and implementers
sections.question: How does a Property Pack retain meaning across professional and technical boundaries?

chapters.title: Information across a transaction
chapters.purpose: Establish what is exchanged and why the model separates source scope from structure.
chapters.question: What does a Property Pack connect?
chapters.scope: Transaction participants, 451-item scope, property identity, provenance and current status.

topics.title: One property, several professional questions
topics.description: How a shared pack connects a property's information across a transaction while preserving different responsibilities.
topics.prompt: Explain how the Property Pack connects information across a transaction, for property professionals.
topics.contribution: A temporal account suits video; both native styles explain the same subject.

chapters.title: Reading the ontology
chapters.purpose: Build a connected understanding of the model and the practical route from source item to constraint.
chapters.question: How do source questions become resources, relationships and rules?
chapters.scope: Classes, identifiers, object and datatype properties, consolidation, vocabularies, shapes, glossary, dictionary and coverage.

topics.title: From a source question to a connected model
topics.description: The complete model-reading account, including Property and Address, utility consolidation and validation examples.
topics.prompt: Explain how the Property Pack ontology represents source questions as resources, relationships, vocabularies and constraints, for domain specialists and implementers.
topics.contribution: A long deck supports inspection of related constructs and the full semantic package.

chapters.title: Meaning and semantic ownership
chapters.purpose: Make the model's boundaries and reuse relationships visible without inventing mappings.
chapters.question: Who owns a meaning, and how can other contexts use it?
chapters.scope: Six property contexts, scheme context, common boundary, direct relationships and absent governed mappings.

topics.title: The semantic homes of the Property Pack
topics.description: The ownership and reuse distinctions behind the six property contexts, scheme context and common boundary.
topics.prompt: Explain the semantic homes and reuse relationships of the Property Pack ontology, for domain reviewers.
topics.contribution: A spatial comparison suits an infographic. Six variants retain identical source selection and prompt.

chapters.title: Validation, judgement and release
chapters.purpose: Equip reviewers to separate executable checks from decisions about meaning and adoption.
chapters.question: What is proved by validation, and what still needs human judgement?
chapters.scope: Coverage, SHACL probes, competency queries, standards limits, technical determination and proposed migration.

topics.title: When is a model ready to rely on?
topics.description: A discussion of what passing tests establish, what remains disputed and how a determination differs from a release.
topics.prompt: Explain what Property Pack validation proves and what still needs human judgement, for technical and domain reviewers.
topics.contribution: Brief, Deep Dive and Debate offer different listening accounts of a consequential judgement.
